request.spec:
Each sheet has a "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there. It starts as the real
date. Every decision in the app that depends on the date, and every default date, uses the
sheet's today and never the real clock.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each sheet has a "today" date, shown on the screen and changeable there. It starts as the real
date. Every decision in the app that depends on the date, and every default date, uses the
sheet's today and never the real clock.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each sheet now has its own "today", shown on the screen and changeable there, and `bin/e2e` passes. The test sets the date to 2026-03-10, then 2024-02-29, and after each reload sees the stored date.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V2__sheet_today.sql`, adds a required `today` column to `sheet`. A new sheet starts with the real date, and any sheets that already existed are set to the current date.
- **Server:** loading a sheet now returns its today as well. A new `PUT /api/sheets/{id}/today` changes it, rejecting a missing or badly formed date. `SheetService.today(id)` gives other code the sheet's date to use in place of the clock. I added `SheetNotFoundException` (a 404) for changing the date on a sheet that doesn't exist.
- **Front end:** the session keeps the sheet's today and refreshes it on every load, so a second user sees the change after reloading the sheet. The screen shows `sheet-today` with a date input (`sheet-today-input`) and a `sheet-today-save` button. A blank or rejected date shows the existing `sheet-error` message, which goes away when the date field or the sheet-id field is edited.

The app has no other date-based features or default dates yet, so nothing else needed switching off the real clock. Anything added later should use `SheetService.today(id)` instead. Changing the date writes no audit record, because the spec doesn't expect one.
